mainTopic: Who counts as a ממזר: the three views in the משנה and their sources in one פסוק, plus when a wife's or יבמה's sister becomes permitted
overview: The משנה gives three opinions about which forbidden relationships produce a ממזר. רבי עקיבא says any forbidden close relative, שמעון התימני says any relationship punished by כרת (and the הלכה follows him), and רבי יהושע says only relationships punished by מיתת בית דין. בן עזאי supports רבי יהושע with an old lineage scroll from ירושלים. The משנה then lists cases where a man may marry the sister of his wife or his יבמה once she has died. The גמרא finds all three opinions in one פסוק in דברים: 'A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's cloak,' which sits right next to 'לא יבא ממזר.' רבי עקיבא reads 'his father's cloak' as a לאו-level case, and the wider views of רבי סימאי and רבי ישבב come from the extra 'and' in 'וְלֹא'. שמעון התימני reads it as a כרת-level case. רבי יהושע reads the פסוק as drawing a line at the father's wife. אביי then begins a statement that all the תנאים agree about a נדה, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's definition of a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks who is a ממזר. רבי עקיבא answers: the child of any forbidden close relative under a 'לא יבא' prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is a ממזר? The child of any close relative the Torah forbids with 'he shall not come.' This is רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new topic by asking which forbidden relationships produce a ממזר. רבי עקיבא gives the widest answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not require a severe punishment like כרת or death. For him, the Torah forbidding a close relative (שאר בשר) with a 'לא יבא' prohibition is enough to make the child a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from certain forbidden relationships, who may not marry into the general community
A close blood relative
'He shall not come', the Torah's language for a forbidden relationship
Our משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Not every child born from a forbidden relationship is a ממזר. The whole משנה is a מחלוקת about exactly which relationships count.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Who is a mamzer?
Any close relative
who is under 'he shall not come,'
phrases.notes: Literally 'he shall not come.' It is the Torah's way of saying a relationship is forbidden.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, a ממזר comes from any forbidden close relative under a 'לא יבא' prohibition.

steps.title: שמעון התימני: only relationships punished by כרת
steps.stepSummary: שמעון התימני limits ממזר to relationships punished by כרת, and the משנה rules like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון התימני says a ממזר comes from any relationship that is punished by כרת at the hands of Heaven, and the הלכה follows him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion narrows the definition. Only relationships punished by כרת produce a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is narrower than רבי עקיבא's view, because a plain prohibition is not enough. Every relationship punished by מיתת בית דין also carries כרת, so his list includes those too. The משנה itself states that the הלכה follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: Being 'cut off', a punishment from Heaven
By the hands of Heaven, not by a human court
And the practical law follows his words

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה: a ממזר is the child of a relationship punished by כרת.

phrases.english: Shimon HaTimni says:
any relationship for which one is liable
karet at the hands of Heaven,
and the halacha follows his words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא and narrows the category
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממזר comes only from relationships punished by כרת, and the הלכה follows this view.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: only relationships punished by court-imposed death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע gives the narrowest definition. Only relationships punished by מיתת בית דין produce a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says a ממזר comes only from a relationship that is punished by death by the court.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion narrows the definition even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some relationships carry כרת but no court death penalty. Those would produce a ממזר according to שמעון התימני but not according to רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: The death penalty carried out by a court

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels, from widest to narrowest: רבי עקיבא (any forbidden relative), שמעון התימני (כרת), רבי יהושע (court death). The הלכה follows שמעון התימני.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua says:
any relationship for which one is liable
death by the court.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממזר comes only from relationships punished by מיתת בית דין.

steps.title: בן עזאי's lineage scroll supports רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי found a lineage scroll in ירושלים that called someone a ממזר from a married woman. This supports רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said: I found a family-lineage scroll in ירושלים. It said, 'So-and-so is a ממזר from a married woman.' This supports רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי brings evidence from an old document to back up רבי יהושע's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with a married woman are punished by מיתת בית דין. The scroll specifically named that as the reason this man was a ממזר, which fits רבי יהושע's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A scroll recording family lineages
So-and-so, an unnamed person
A married woman
To uphold or support

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said:
I found a scroll of family lineages in Jerusalem,
and it was written in it:
So-and-so is a mamzer from a married woman,
to uphold the words of Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע's view that a ממזר comes from relationships punished by מיתת בית דין
steps.raayaSupportSource: An old lineage scroll from ירושלים that named a married woman as the source of someone's ממזר status

steps.title: A wife's sister is permitted after the wife dies
steps.stepSummary: In three cases the wife has died: she died while married, she died after he divorced her, or she died after marrying someone else. In each case he may marry her sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his wife died, he may marry her sister. If he divorced her and she died, he may marry her sister. If she married someone else and died, he may marry her sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new rule about the wife's sister. Once the wife has died, her sister is permitted to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a wife's sister lasts only while the wife is alive. Divorce or her remarriage does not change this. What matters is that she has died.

keyTerms.meaning: He is permitted to her sister
He divorced her
She married another man

steps.confusionAlert: Divorce alone does not permit the sister. Every case here ends with 'and she died.'

phrases.english: If his wife died,
he is permitted to her sister.
If he divorced her and she died,
he is permitted to her sister.
If she married another and died,
he is permitted to her sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the wife has died, in any of these situations, her sister is permitted to him.

steps.title: A יבמה's sister is permitted after the יבמה dies
steps.stepSummary: The same three cases are repeated for a יבמה: she died, she died after חליצה, or she died after marrying someone else. In each case her sister is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his יבמה died, he may marry her sister. If he did חליצה with her and she died, he may marry her sister. If she married someone else and died, he may marry her sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same rule to a יבמה, the widow of his brother who died without children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The connection to a יבמה forbids him from her sister, just as with a wife. Once the יבמה dies, that ban ends, whether or not חליצה was done.

keyTerms.meaning: His יבמה, the widow of his brother who died childless
He performed חליצה with her, releasing her from יבום

steps.whatToRemember: The sister of a wife or יבמה is forbidden only while the wife or יבמה is alive. Once she dies, the sister is permitted.

phrases.english: If his yevama died,
he is permitted to her sister.
If he performed chalitza with her and she died,
he is permitted to her sister.
If she married another and died,
he is permitted to her sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same rule, applied to a יבמה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the יבמה has died, her sister is permitted, even after חליצה or after she remarried.

steps.title: What is רבי עקיבא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי עקיבא's wide definition of ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking where רבי עקיבא gets his view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's view is the widest of the three, so the גמרא wants to see which פסוק supports it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי עקיבא's opinion in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי עקיבא's definition of ממזר

steps.title: The verse about the father's cloak
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's cloak.' It reads this as: a woman his father was with, the son may not uncover.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's cloak.' This means: a 'cloak' that his father saw, the son may not uncover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering with a פסוק. It explains the phrase 'his father's cloak' to mean a woman his father had relations with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Cloak' is understood as a woman connected to the father, and the son is forbidden to her. The גמרא is laying the groundwork for רבי עקיבא's source, and the full connection to ממזר comes in what follows.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
His father's cloak, here meaning a woman connected to his father
He shall not uncover

phrases.english: As it is written:
"A man shall not take his father's wife,
and he shall not uncover his father's cloak."
A cloak that his father saw,
phrases.notes: 'Saw' here is a gentle way of saying the father had relations with her.

phrases.english: he may not uncover.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about רבי עקיבא's source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about not uncovering the father's 'cloak', read as a woman the father was with. This begins the source for רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא follows רבי יהודה: the פסוק is about a woman raped by his father
steps.stepSummary: The answer continues. רבי עקיבא holds like רבי יהודה, who says the פסוק of 'his father's cloak' speaks about אנוסת אביו, a woman his father raped. Relations with her are forbidden only by a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds like רבי יהודה, who said: the פסוק is talking about a woman raped by his father, and she is one of the women forbidden only by a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the answer from step 8. It explains which woman the פסוק 'he shall not uncover his father's cloak' is talking about, according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק the way רבי יהודה does: it is about a woman his father was with, namely אנוסת אביו. Relations with her are forbidden by a לאו, not punished with כרת. This sets up the proof that a לאו-level relationship can produce a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman whom one's father raped (not married to him)
the פסוק is speaking about
relationships forbidden by a negative commandment (a לאו), not punished by כרת

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'his father's wife' with 'a woman raped by his father.' In רבי יהודה's reading, this פסוק is about the raped woman, which is only a לאו.

phrases.english: And he holds like Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
phrases.notes: 'He' means רבי עקיבא, whose reasoning we have been explaining since step 7.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking about a woman raped by his father,
who is among those for whom one is liable for violating a prohibition (לאו),

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer of step 8 by identifying which woman the פסוק refers to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of 'his father's cloak' refers to אנוסת אביו, a לאו-level prohibition, following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A פסוק close by says 'a ממזר shall not enter', so a לאו relationship makes a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: Right next to the פסוק about his father's raped woman comes 'לא יבא ממזר בקהל ה׳'. Because the two פסוקים are side by side, a child from a לאו-level relationship is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And right next to it is the פסוק 'A ממזר shall not enter the congregation of ה׳.' This shows that from these relationships, a ממזר is born.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof for רבי עקיבא. It points out that a פסוק just after it, with only one other פסוק in between, is about a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two פסוקים sit next to each other, the גמרא connects them. The first speaks of a לאו-level forbidden woman, and the next forbids a ממזר. So a child from a relationship forbidden only by a לאו is a ממזר, which is רבי עקיבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: right next to it (a פסוק placed beside another, which teaches a connection)
apparently, this shows that
the congregation of ה׳ (here: marrying into the Jewish people)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's source: the פסוק about אנוסת אביו (a לאו) sits right next to 'לא יבא ממזר', so a לאו-level relationship produces a ממזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the full reason why רבי עקיבא counts children of לאו-level relationships as ממזרים, not only children of כרת-level relationships.

phrases.english: And right next to it is written:
"A mamzer shall not enter the congregation of the Lord,"
apparently, from these relationships the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation begun in steps 8 and 9 by connecting the neighboring פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because 'לא יבא ממזר' sits beside the פסוק about a לאו-level woman, a child from a לאו-level relationship is a ממזר.

steps.title: What is the source according to רבי סימאי and רבי ישבב?
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי says רבי עקיבא includes all לאו-level relationships, even with non-relatives. רבי ישבב says he includes even relationships forbidden by an עשה. These are not like a father's raped woman, so where do they come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי סימאי, who includes other לאו-level relationships that are not with a relative, and according to רבי ישבב, who includes even relationships forbidden by a positive commandment (עשה), what is the source?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. The source we just learned covers a relative forbidden by a לאו, so what about the wider views of רבי סימאי and רבי ישבב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אנוסת אביו is a close relative forbidden by a לאו. רבי סימאי adds לאו cases that are not relatives, and רבי ישבב adds even עשה cases. Neither fits the case in the פסוק, so the source from steps 8-10 is not enough for them.

keyTerms.meaning: includes (adds more cases to the rule)
a close blood relative
relationships forbidden by a positive commandment (an עשה)

steps.confusionAlert: Two words look almost the same: שְׁאָר means 'other' and שְׁאֵר means 'a close relative.' Both appear in this line.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Simai, who includes
other relationships forbidden by a prohibition that are not with a relative,
and according to Rabbi Yeshevav, who includes
even relationships forbidden by a positive commandment —
phrases.notes: The question 'what is their source?' is not written out, but it is understood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי סִימַאי, דִּמְרַבֵּה שְׁאָר חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the wider versions of רבי עקיבא's view can be supported, since the derivation in steps 9-10 only covers a relative forbidden by a לאו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for including non-relative לאו cases (רבי סימאי) and עשה cases (רבי ישבב) as ממזר.

steps.title: They learn it from the extra word 'and' in 'וְלֹא'
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי and רבי ישבב learn the extra cases from the word 'and' in 'and he shall not uncover his father's cloak.' The extra letter adds more cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from the word 'and he shall not.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 11. The wider cases come from the extra 'and' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said just 'לא' ('he shall not'), but it says 'וְלֹא' ('and he shall not'). That extra ו is read as adding more cases beyond his father's raped woman. This covers the wider lists of רבי סימאי and רבי ישבב.

keyTerms.meaning: they derive it, they learn it out
'and not'; the extra ו (and) is read as including more cases

steps.whatToRemember: The basic source for רבי עקיבא is the פסוק next to 'לא יבא ממזר'. The wider views of רבי סימאי and רבי ישבב rely on the extra ו of 'וְלֹא'.

phrases.english: They derive it from "and he shall not."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:1: 'and he shall not uncover his father's cloak.' The extra 'and' adds more cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by finding an extra word in the פסוק that includes the wider cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו in 'וְלֹא' includes non-relative לאו cases and even עשה cases.

steps.title: שמעון התימני's source: only כרת-level relationships make a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: שמעון התימני agrees with the רבנן that 'his father's cloak' speaks about a woman waiting for his father's יבום. That relationship carries כרת. Since 'לא יבא ממזר' sits right next to it, a ממזר comes from כרת-level relationships.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמעון התימני holds like the רבנן, who say the פסוק speaks about a woman waiting for his father to do יבום. Relations with her carry כרת. Right next to it is 'A ממזר shall not enter.' So a child from a כרת-level relationship is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives שמעון התימני's source. He reads the same פסוק as רבי עקיבא, but he understands 'his father's cloak' as a different woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא, like רבי יהודה, read 'his father's cloak' as a woman forbidden only by a לאו, so even a לאו makes a ממזר. שמעון התימני follows the רבנן, who read it as a שומרת יבם of his father, whose relationship carries כרת. Using the same 'side by side' method, he sets the minimum level for ממזר at כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום
Relationships whose punishment is כרת
Apparently / this shows that

phrases.english: And Shimon HaTimni holds like the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: בְּשׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם שֶׁל אָבִיו הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: who say: the verse is speaking about a woman waiting for his father to do levirate marriage,
phrases.notes: She is the widow of his father's brother. Since his father's brother's wife is forbidden to him, being with her carries כרת.

phrases.english: so she is one of the relationships that carry karet,
and right next to it is: "A mamzer shall not enter."
This shows: from karet-level relationships, the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבי עקיבא's source, the גמרא gives the source for the second view in the משנה, using the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמעון התימני reads 'his father's cloak' as a שומרת יבם of his father, a כרת-level relationship, and learns from the side-by-side פסוקים that ממזר comes from כרת-level relationships.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's source: only the father's-wife level makes a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע argues that if the Torah meant to include lighter cases, it would only need to write 'shall not uncover.' Writing 'shall not take his father's wife' too shows a limit: only the case between those words, the father's wife, makes a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע? Let the Torah write only 'shall not uncover.' Why do I need 'shall not take'? Rather, this is what it means: the case from 'shall not take' until 'shall not uncover' makes a ממזר; beyond that, no ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the third view, רבי יהושע, who holds a ממזר comes only from relationships punished by מיתת בית דין. He reads the פסוק as drawing a line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father's wife is stricter (מיתת בית דין) than whoever 'his father's cloak' refers to. If a ממזר came even from the lighter case, the stricter case would be obvious, so the Torah would not need to write it. Since the Torah does write 'shall not take his father's wife,' רבי יהושע learns that only that level makes a ממזר, and the 'cloak' case beyond it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Why do I need it? (the Torah wrote something that seems extra)
Rather, is it not that...
More / beyond

steps.whatToRemember: Three views, one פסוק: רבי עקיבא (even a לאו makes a ממזר), שמעון התימני (only כרת), רבי יהושע (only מיתת בית דין, like a father's wife).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua:
Let the Merciful One write only "he shall not uncover."
phrases.notes: If even the lighter 'cloak' case made a ממזר, the stricter case of his father's wife would be obvious.

phrases.english: Why do I need "shall not take" (and "shall not uncover")?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. Either way, the question is about why 'shall not take' is written.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: מִ״לֹּא יִקַּח״ עַד ״לֹא יְגַלֶּה״ — הָוֵי מַמְזֵר,
phrases.english: from "shall not take" until "shall not uncover" is a mamzer,
phrases.notes: The woman between those words is his father's wife.

phrases.english: beyond that is not a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא לֹא יְגַלֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the third and final view in the משנה, completing the three-way explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seemingly extra words 'shall not take his father's wife' limit ממזר to the father's-wife level (מיתת בית דין); the 'cloak' case beyond it does not make a ממזר.

steps.title: אביי begins: everyone agrees about one who is with a נדה
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens a new statement: all the תנאים agree about a case of one who has relations with a נדה. The rest of his statement follows next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees about one who has relations with a נדה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement from אביי, telling us that all the views agree about a נדה. This line sets up the ruling he gives next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three views just explained disagree about how strict a relationship must be to make a ממזר. A נדה carries כרת, so you might think the views would argue about it. אביי begins to say that here there is agreement, and the ruling itself continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
A woman in her menstrual state, forbidden with a punishment of כרת

phrases.english: Abaye said:
All agree about one who has relations with a menstruating woman,
phrases.notes: 'All' means all the תנאים in the משנה. His sentence continues right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all three sources are explained, אביי opens a new point about where the views agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the תנאים agree regarding one who is with a נדה; the content of the agreement follows in the continuation.
